text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government's new proposals to liberalise labour laws indicate a complete rejection by the state of union policy.
- Opposition parties are angry at the government's failure to inform them of the expulsion of a Swede for alleged spying in Russia.
- The government and the national competition board are at loggerheads over whether or not local governments should be allowed to own private companies.
- The suspected Swedish spy who allegedly received secret Russian documents is to have acted on assignment from the Swedish secret defence agency, KSI.
- The newspaper, hit by a stagnating market, must shed some 125 jobs.
- One in ten Swedes over 75 years old contemplates suicide at some time, a survey shows.

- Volvo is reportedly in talks with the government of Karnataka, a province in southern India, over setting up a joint venture in the province to manufacture low-floor buses for the city of Bangalore.
- The Swedish Trade Union Confederation (LO) is to present to the government measures to cut unemployment, such as investment grants to stimulate the construction industry.
